Incus has an arbitrary file write on host via `exec-output` symlink in crafted image

Aliases: CVE-2026-48750

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/lxc/incus/v7/cmd/incusd — fixed in 7.2.0

### Summary The `record-output` parameter of the `/instances/$name/exec` endpoint stores the output of the command in the `exec-output` directory of the instance. golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent doesn't enforce invoking key constraints

Aliases: CVE-2026-39833, GO-2026-5005

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-w879-237q-wc7r: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Invoking pathological RSA/DSA parameters may cause DoS
entry.content:
golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Invoking pathological RSA/DSA parameters may cause DoS

Aliases: CVE-2026-39829, GO-2026-5018

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • golang.org/x/crypto/ssh — fixed in 0.52.0

The RSA and DSA public key parsers did not enforce size limits on key parameters. A crafted public key with an excessively large modulus or DSA parameter could cause several minutes of CPU consumption during signature verification. This could be triggered by unauthenticated clients during public key authentication. RSA moduli are now limited to 8192 bits, and DSA parameters are validated per FIPS 186-2.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-89gr-r52h-f8rx: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: FIDO/U2F security key physical presence check can be bypassed
entry.content:
golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: FIDO/U2F security key physical presence check can be bypassed

Aliases: CVE-2026-39831, GO-2026-5019

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • golang.org/x/crypto/ssh — fixed in 0.52.0

The Verify() method for FIDO/U2F security key types (sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com, sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com) did not check the User Presence flag. Signatures generated without physical touch were accepted, allowing unattended use of a hardware security key. To restore the previous behavior, return a "no-touch-required" extension in Permissions.Extensions from PublicKeyCallback.

entry.content:
Fleet Affected by Local Privilege Escalation via Tcl Command Injection in Orbit

Aliases: CVE-2026-27806, GO-2026-5634

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/fleetdm/fleet/v4 — fixed in 4.81.1

## Summary The Orbit agent's FileVault disk encryption key rotation flow on collects a local user's password via a GUI dialog and interpolates it directly into a Tcl/expect script executed via `exec.Command("expect", "-c", script)`. Because the password is inserted into Tcl brace-quoted `send {%s}`, a password containing `}` terminates the literal and injects arbitrary Tcl commands. Since Orbit runs as root, this allows a local unprivileged user to escalate to root privileges. ## CWE - **CWE-78**: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') - **CWE-94**: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') ## Impact - Local privilege escalation to root: Any unprivileged local user on a managed endpoint can execute arbitrary commands …
